reportId.description:
The unique identifier (primary key) of the pre-configured report that will be generated. This references a report that has been created and configured in the Origami reporting system.
More info...

Reports are pre-configured in the Origami system through the Reports administration interface (available to users with the appropriate permissions). Each report:

  • Created by administrators or power users — Built using the system's report designer.
  • Stored in the Reports table — Each has a unique ReportID (primary key).
  • Associated with domains — Configured to work with specific entity types (Claim, Policy, etc.).
  • Has templates — Defines layout, columns, grouping, filtering, and formatting.

How to Find Report IDs

Via UI: Navigate to the Reports section → View/Edit a report → The ID appears in the URL or record details.

Via API: Use the /api/v1/Reports endpoint to list available reports.

Common Method: System administrators typically provide Report IDs for automation or integrations.

matchField.description:
Definition:
If matchField is provided, the system passes the domainKey value to the report with explicit instructions to apply an equality filter (exact match) using the field name you supplied. In effect, the report is limited to records where {matchField} = {domainKey}.
Example: domainKey = 12345 and matchField = "ClaimID" causes the report to run with ClaimID = 12345.

More info...

When matchField is omitted

No record-specific filter is sent to the report. The report executes only with its own preconfigured filters and has no awareness of the triggering record (for example, it does not automatically limit to ClaimID = 12345). The domainKey is still used by the action for other purposes, such as attaching the generated file to the parent record when attachToParent = true and resolving form tags in file names, subjects, and bodies, but the report content itself is not scoped to that record.

Why it matters

This mechanism is essential for reports that read from child or related entities (for example, payments, notes, documents). Providing matchField ensures the output is narrowed to the triggering record rather than returning broader, multi-record results.

Requirements and behavior

  • matchField must name a field that exists in the report's dataset for the specified reportId.
  • The field name is case-sensitive and must match exactly as defined in the report.
  • The system searches for the field in the report's available fields. If not found, it retries briefly, then proceeds without applying the filter (no error is thrown).

Practical example

A) With matchField

Inputs: domainKey = 12345, matchField = "ClaimID"
Effect on report: Applies ClaimID = 12345, so detail tables, totals, and sections are scoped to Claim #12345.
Other uses of domainKey: Resolves form tags and attaches the generated file to Claim #12345 if attachToParent = true.

B) Without matchField

Inputs: domainKey = 12345, matchField not provided
Effect on report: No ClaimID filter is applied; the report runs with only its built-in filters and has no direct context linking it to Claim #12345.
Other uses of domainKey: Still used to resolve form tags and attach the generated file to Claim #12345 if attachToParent = true.

Key takeaways

  • matchField controls whether the report receives a record-specific filter derived from domainKey.
  • domainKey always supplies context to the action (form tags, attachment target, execution context), but it only constrains the report's data when matchField names a valid field in the report dataset.

format.description: Specifies what file type the report should be generated as.

fileName.description:
Specifies the filename for the generated report file. Supports form tags for dynamic naming based on record data.

  • Extension is optional: Filenames may be provided with or without an extension.
  • System adds extension automatically: The system appends the correct extension based on the format parameter if none is provided.
  • Conflict resolution: If the supplied extension conflicts with the selected format, the system replaces apply the correct extension based on the selected format value.

attachToParent.description: Controls whether the generated report file is saved and attached to the parent record (specified by domainName and domainKey). When enabled, creates a File record in the system and associates it with the triggering record.

description.description: Sets the description/comment field for the generated file when it's attached to the parent record. This description appears in file listings and provides context about what the file contains or why it was generated.  Only applies when `attachToParent: true`. If the report is only emailed or faxed without being attached to the record, this parameter has no effect.

folderId.description:
Only used when `attachToParent: true`. Specifies which folder to place the generated report file in when attaching it to the parent record. This determines the organizational structure and categorization of the attached file.
Default Behavior (if not provided):
The system uses the default folder configuration for the domain/record type, or places the file in the root level if no default is configured.

documentTypeId.description:
Optional (only used when `attachToParent: true`). 

This is a numeric value passed as a string. It specifies the document type classification for the generated report file when attaching it to the parent record. This sets the file's type categorization for organizational and filtering purposes.

If the report is not being attached to the record, this parameter is ignored.

Purpose:

documentStatusId.description:
Optional (only used when `attachToParent: true`). Specifies the document status classification for the generated report file when attaching it to the parent record. This sets the file's status for workflow and lifecycle management purposes. If the report is not being attached to the record, this parameter is ignored. Document statuses are pre-configured in the system through the DocumentStatuses administration interface. Common statuses include:
• Draft
• Under Review
• Approved
• Final
• Archived
• Rejected

categories.description:
Specifies one or more category classifications for the generated report file when it is attached to the parent record. Categories provide additional tagging and organizational capabilities beyond document type and status.

Only applies when attachToParent: true. If the report is not being attached to the record, this parameter is ignored.

More info...

Use categories to add cross-cutting labels that aid discovery, governance, and workflow decisions. These labels are distinct from document type and status, and can be combined to reflect multiple dimensions such as confidentiality, audience, and regulatory needs.

Format

Comma-separated list of category IDs (strings):

  • Single category: 5
  • Multiple categories: 5,12,18
Default Behavior

If not provided, the file is attached without specific category classifications.

Examples
  • Single category
  • Multiple categories

Categories are pre-configured in the system through the Categories administration interface. Common examples include:

  • Legal Documents
  • Customer Communications
  • Internal Use Only
  • Regulatory Required
  • Financial Reports
  • Confidential

to.description: Optional. If not provided, the report is not emailed. This is the fully qualified email address of the recipient who will receive the email. Supports multiple recipients provided as a comma‑separated list. Form tags are supported, for example {Claim.Adjuster.Email}.

noSendIfEmptyTo.description:
If all recipient fields resolve to empty values after form tag processing, the action silently succeeds. This behavior results in the following:

  • No email is sent
  • Email generation returns null without throwing an exception
  • The surrounding event or workflow continues without failure

This prevents the email action from causing an error when the to, cc, and bcc fields all resolve to empty strings. It is especially useful when recipients are supplied via dynamic form tags that may not always have values.

cc.description: Fully qualified email address of the Cc recipient(s). Supports multiple recipients provided as a comma‑separated list. Form tags are supported, for example {Claim.Adjuster.Email}.

bcc.description: Fully qualified email address of the Bcc recipient(s). Supports multiple recipients provided as a comma‑separated list. Form tags are supported, for example {Claim.Adjuster.Email}.

body.description: This is the body of the email that will be sent. Supports html markup and {formTag} resolution.

replyTo.description: Email address that will receive replies to the message. If provided, this value overrides the default sender reply‑to address. Supports a single valid email address and form tags, such as {User.Email}.

faxNumber.description: If provided, this value is used as the fax destination number. All standard phone number formats are supported, including country codes, area codes, and formatted numbers. Form tags are also supported, such as {Contact.FaxNumber}.

faxTo.description:
If `faxNumber` has been provided, the `faxTo` value will be rendered onto the fax's cover page for better recipient identification.

Form tags are supported, for example {Contact.FullName}.

faxBody.description:
This value specifies the content for the fax cover page. This optional field allows you to include a message or instructions that will appear as the first page of the fax transmission, before the generated document attachment.

Form tags are supported, for example {Contact.FullName}. HTML markup is also supported.

dispositionEmail.description: Email address to receive fax status notifications. Only one (1) email address can be provided.

dispositionLevel.description: Applicable only when a `dispositionEmail` value has been provided. Specifies which fax transmission status notifications are sent to the `dispositionEmail` address. Controls whether the eFax service sends notifications only for failed transmissions (Error) or for all outcomes (All, including success and failure).

faxAttachFilesFromFolderId.description: Attaches existing files from a specified folder on the parent record to the outgoing fax. Files are retrieved, converted to fax-compatible formats, and included with the fax transmission.

emailTypeId.description:
Email Type Classification

Specifies the email type classification when emailing the generated report. This parameter is only relevant when email parameters (to, subject, body) are provided.

When Used

Only applies when sending the report via email. If the report is only being generated or attached (attachToParent: true) without emailing, this parameter is ignored.

Recommendation

Optional but strongly recommended when emailing reports.

  • You can omit emailTypeId if:
    • The user has full email access (admin or unrestricted), or
    • The user’s EmailRole has CanAccessEmailsWithoutEmailType = true
  • You must provide emailTypeId if:
    • The user has restricted email access (assigned to an EmailRole), and
    • The EmailRole has CanAccessEmailsWithoutEmailType = false or null

Omitting this value when required may cause the action to queue, but it can still fail at runtime due to a security or permission error.

attachFilesFromFolderId.description:
Optional parameter that specifies a Folder ID. When provided, all files from that folder will be attached to the email.
Important: If any of the following inputs are provided, they take precedence and `attachFilesFromFolderId` is completely ignored:
• `attachFilesFromFilter`
• `attachFilesFromParentFilter`
• `attachStaticFiles`

attachFilesFromFilter.description:
Optional parameter that accepts a filter expression string to specify which files attached to the domain record should be automatically attached to the email. Uses Origami's Advanced Search filter syntax.

`1)` Applies the filter expression to the File records attached to the domain record
`2)`Retrieves all files matching the filter criteria
`3)`Automatically attaches those files to the outgoing email

Attachment Aggregation Rules
Files selected by this parameter are added cumulatively with files produced by the other attachment filtering mechanisms. All files are combined and deduplicated prior to sending the email. The final set of attached files is the union of files returned by the following parameters:
`attachFilesFromFilter`, `attachFilesFromParentFilter`, and `attachStaticFiles`

If the same file is selected by more than one of these sources, it is included only once in the outgoing email.

attachFilesFromParentFilter.description:
An Origami Advanced Search filter expression to attach files from parent records of the triggering entity. Uses the same filter syntax as `attachFilesFromFilter`, but searches in the parent record(s) instead of the current record.

When this parameter is provided:

`1)` Identifies all parent records linked to the triggering entity (via the Link table)
`2)` For each parent that supports file attachments (`HasFiles=true`)
`3)` Applies the filter expression to find matching files attached to that parent
`4)` Returns the union of all matching files from all parents

Attachment Aggregation Rules
Files selected by this parameter are added cumulatively with files produced by the other attachment filtering mechanisms. All files are combined and deduplicated prior to sending the email. The final set of attached files is the union of files returned by the following parameters:
`attachFilesFromFilter`, `attachFilesFromParentFilter`, and `attachStaticFiles`

If the same file is selected by more than one of these sources, it is included only once in the outgoing email.

attachStaticFiles.description:
A comma-separated list of File IDs representing specific files that already exist in the Origami system. These files will be attached to the email regardless of their location or parent record. The files are directly referenced by their corresponding `FileID`.

Attachment Aggregation Rules
Files selected by this parameter are added cumulatively with files produced by the other attachment filtering mechanisms. All files are combined and deduplicated prior to sending the email. The final set of attached files is the union of files returned by the following parameters:
`attachFilesFromFilter`, `attachFilesFromParentFilter`, and `attachStaticFiles`

If the same file is selected by more than one of these sources, it is included only once in the outgoing email.

trackReplies.description:
Enables reply tracking for the email, allowing the system to capture and record recipient responses as new Email records in Origami. When enabled, the system generates a unique tracking address that recipient replies are sent to, which then get processed and attached to the original email's parent record.

Important Notes
• System Configuration Required - Email infrastructure must be configured to receive emails at the tracking address domain.
• Recorded Emails Only - Only works if system is configured to record outgoing emails (RecordOutgoingEmails setting)
• Thread Matching - Replies are matched by ThreadGuid, not email subject or message threading
• File Attachments - Reply email attachments are automatically processed and attached to the reply Email record

sendUnsecure.description:
Bypasses email encryption and sends the email without secure/encrypted delivery, even when encryption is configured for the system. This parameter allows users with proper permissions to override encryption settings on a per-email basis.

Important Notes
• Audit Trail - The SendUnsecure value is stored on the Email record for compliance auditing
• Permission Required - Users must have explicit permission to send unsecured emails
• System Override - Some email templates can force encryption (SecureEmailOption = "F") which prevents this parameter from working

usePlainText.description:
Controls whether the email is sent as plain text or HTML. When set to true, the email body is sent as plain text without HTML formatting. When false (default), the email supports HTML markup.

Form Tags: Both plain text and HTML bodies support Origami form tags (e.g., {ClaimNumber}, {UserEmail})
Automatic Encoding: When HTML mode is on, plain text content is automatically HTML-encoded to prevent formatting issues

doNotRecordEmail.description:
Prevents the system from creating an Email record in the database for this sent email. When set to true, the email is sent but no record is saved to the Emails table or linked to the parent record.

Important: This parameter only has effect when the system-wide setting RecordOutgoingEmails is enabled.

excludeGlobalSignature.description: When set to `true`, the global email signature that would normally be appended to all outgoing emails from the system is ommitted.

priority.description:
The priority parameter is a boolean flag that marks the email as high priority, which affects how the email appears to recipients in the email client.

When set to `true`, the email is sent with high priority status, which typically displays a red exclamation mark or similar indicator in most email clients to signal urgency to recipients.

If priority is `false` or omitted (default), emails are sent with normal priority

attachExceededHandling.description:
"0" - Default behavior when attachments exceed limits
"1" - Sends email and creates a notification for the triggering user
"2" - Skips sending, creates draft email on parent record, and notifies* the triggering user

*Notifications include:Client name, Event description, Domain and record ID, Action name, Recipient emails, A link to the event.

Important Notes
• `Parameter Required`: Size checking only occurs if attachExceededHandling is provided (not null/empty)
• `Default Strip Behavior`: When unconfigured but limit exceeded, attachments are automatically stripped and email still sends
• `Option 2 Creates Draft`: When "2" is used, email content is saved as a draft record on the parent entity for reference
• `System Users Excluded`: Notification emails are NOT sent if event was triggered by a system process user
• `Link Alternative`: System may convert attachments to download links if SendAttachmentsAsLinksIfExceedMaxSize is enabled
• `Attachment Types`: Only applies to actual file attachments, not inline images or embedded content
• `Multiple Attachment Sources`: All attachment sources (folder, filter, parent filter, static files) are included in size calculation

autoFillMappingSetName.description:
AutoFill Mapping Set

Specifies the name of a predefined AutoFill mapping set used to automatically populate fields in a newly created RootCause record. The mapping pulls values from the parent record identified by domainName and domainKey.

A mapping set defines how data flows from a source domain (the parent record type) to a target domain (RootCause). When a valid mapping set name is provided, the system applies all configured field-to-field mappings during RootCause creation.

More info... How to Find Valid Mapping Set Names

You can retrieve available mapping sets using:

OrigamiApi/api/AutoFillMappingSet/Query?filter=TargetDomain.Name:eq:RootCause

In the response, the Name field identifies the mapping set to reference. Example:

{
"Name": "ClaimToRootCause",
"Description": "Maps claim data to root cause fields",

}

revokeDate.description:
The revokeDate parameter accepts multiple value formats for specifying when external access should expire.
See examples... ##### 1. Relative Date Math (Recommended) Uses + or - with a number and optional unit suffix. "revokeDate": "+30" // 30 days from now (days is the default unit)
"revokeDate": "+30d" // 30 days from now
"revokeDate": "+2w" // 2 weeks from now
"revokeDate": "+6m" // 6 months from now
"revokeDate": "+1y" // 1 year from now
"revokeDate": "-7d" // 7 days ago **Time-of-day Units** "revokeDate": "+24h" // 24 hours from now
"revokeDate": "+30n" // 30 minutes from now
"revokeDate": "+3600s" // 3600 seconds (1 hour) from now **Period Boundaries** "revokeDate": "+1bm" // First day of next month
"revokeDate": "+0em" // Last day of this month
"revokeDate": "+1bq" // First day of next quarter
"revokeDate": "+0eq" // Last day of this quarter
"revokeDate": "+1by" // January 1st of next year
"revokeDate": "+0ey" // December 31st of this year
"revokeDate": "+1bw" // Sunday of next week
"revokeDate": "+0ew" // Saturday of this week --- ##### 2. Named Date Keywords "revokeDate": "today"
"revokeDate": "tomorrow"
"revokeDate": "yesterday"
"revokeDate": "first day of this month"
"revokeDate": "last day of next quarter"
"revokeDate": "first day of this year" --- ##### 3. Absolute Dates "revokeDate": "12/31/2026" // MM/dd/yyyy
"revokeDate": "2026-12-31" // ISO 8601 --- ##### 4. Never Expire "revokeDate": null
"revokeDate": "" --- ##### 5. Using relativeToDate "revokeDate": "+1y", "relativeToDate": "{Claim.DateOfLoss}"
"revokeDate": "+90d", "relativeToDate": "{Policy.EffectiveDate}"
"revokeDate": "+0em", "relativeToDate": "{Contract.StartDate}"

relativeToDate.description:
Optional modifier that specifies the base date used for relative revokeDate calculations. Supports form tags that resolve to DateTime values.

See more...

Default Behavior (when omitted or null)

  • Relative date math uses the current date and time as the base.

Example:

"revokeDate": "+30d"
Result: Expires 30 days from now.

When relativeToDate Is Provided

  • Relative calculations use the specified field's date instead of the current date.

Example:

{
  "revokeDate": "+1y",
  "relativeToDate": "{Claim.DateOfLoss}"
}

Result: Access expires 1 year from the claim's date of loss.

parameters.description: The `SendMobileForm` action can operate on **any domain** where mobile data collection makes business sense. Common use cases include sending forms from Claims (to collect accident details from claimants), Policies (to gather application information from insureds), Assets (for inspection reports), or Work Orders (for completion confirmations). The action uses the triggering record (specified by `domainName` and `domainKey`) to provide context for the mobile form and to associate any submitted responses with the appropriate business record.

parameters.name: recordId
parameters.description:
The `recordId` is the **primary key (ID) of the specific record** that triggers the mobile form and serves as the anchor for the entire interaction. This record:

1. **Triggered the action** - The event occurred on this record (e.g., Claim ID 12345 was updated to "Under Investigation" status)

2. **Provides form context** - The mobile form can display information from this record to give recipients context about what they're responding to (e.g., "Please provide details about Claim #12345")

3. **Receives the response data** - When the mobile form is completed and submitted, the response data is associated with and stored against this specific record

4. **Enables form tag resolution** - Dynamic content in the SMS message and mobile form (like {Claim.ClaimNumber} or {Policy.InsuredName}) is resolved using data from this record

**Example:**

When Claim #12345 status changes to "Investigating":
- `domainName: "Claim"`
- `domainKey: 12345` (the specific claim being investigated)
- SMS sent with context: "Please complete this form regarding Claim #12345"
- Mobile form displays relevant claim details for reference
- When submitted, the form response is linked to Claim #12345
- Response data appears in Claim #12345's record for future reference

formId1.description:
The `formId1` value corresponds to a **StateFormType** record configured in the system. Each StateFormType defines:
- Form name and description
- Jurisdiction (state) applicability
- Form template/layout
- Required data fields
- Regulatory category (benefit notice, denial, settlement, etc.)

This is **NOT a static enum** - valid values must be looked up from the system's configured State Form Types. Your Origami Administrator may need to provide these to you.

state1.description:
This value specifies the jurisdiction (state) to use when generating the form referenced by `formId1`. If provided, this will override the claim's default jurisdiction for form selection and generation. Supports `{formTag}` resolution (ie: `{Claim.InjuryState}`).

| Type | Examples | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| US States | `"CA"`, `"PA"`, `"TX"`, `"NY"` | Two-letter US state abbreviations |
| Canadian Provinces | `"ON"`, `"BC"`, `"AB"`, `"QC"` | Two-letter Canadian province abbreviations |
| US Territories | `"PR"`, `"VI"`, `"GU"` | Puerto Rico, Virgin Islands, Guam |
| Federal | `"FED"` or similar | Federal jurisdiction (e.g., FECA, Longshore) |

formId2.description: Specifies a second state form to generate in the same action. Follows the same rules as `formId1`. Allows generating multiple state forms in a single action execution. Useful when claim events require a package of related forms (e.g., benefit approval triggers both a payment notice and a wage statement).

state2.description: This value specifies the jurisdiction (state) to use when generating the form referenced by `formId2`. If provided, this will override the claim's default jurisdiction for form selection and generation. Supports `{formTag}` resolution (ie: `{Claim.InjuryState}`).

formId3.description: Specifies a third state form to generate in the same action. Follows the same rules as `formId2`. Allows generating multiple state forms in a single action execution. Useful when claim events require a package of related forms (e.g., benefit approval triggers both a payment notice and a wage statement).

state3.description: This value specifies the jurisdiction (state) to use when generating the form referenced by `formId3`. If provided, this will override the claim's default jurisdiction for form selection and generation. Supports `{formTag}` resolution (ie: `{Claim.InjuryState}`).

flatten.description: Controls whether the generated state form PDF is flattened, making form fields non-editable.

previewWatermark.description: Controls whether the generated state form includes a "PREVIEW" or "DRAFT" watermark overlay, indicating the document is not a final/official version.

sendEmail.description: Controls whether the generated state form(s) are sent via email after generation.

subject.description: Conditional (required when `sendEmail: true`). Defines the subject line for the email used to distribute the generated state form(s) when email distribution is enabled. Supports `{formTag}` resolution for dynamic values.

doNotRecordEmail.description:
Conditional (required when `sendEmail: true`). Controls whether the sent email is recorded in the claim’s correspondence history when email distribution is enabled. When set to `true`, the email is delivered but not logged in the claim record.

What “recording” means (ie `doNotRecordEmail: false`)
- The email appears in the claim’s correspondence and email history.
- Subject, recipients, timestamp, and body are logged.
- Attachments are referenced in the history.
- An audit trail is created for claim communications.

attachStaticFiles.description: Conditional (required when `sendEmail: true`). A comma-separated list of File IDs representing specific files that already exist in the Origami system. These files will be attached to the email regardless of their location or parent record. The files are directly referenced by their corresponding FileID.

attachExceededHandling.description:
Conditional (required when `sendEmail: true`). `"" (empty)` or `null` -- Default: Send email without attachments (standard behavior)
`1` -- Send & Notify: Send email without attachments AND notify* the user who triggered the event
`2` -- Notify But Don't Send: Do NOT send email, create draft email record on parent, AND notify* the user

*Notifications include:Client name, Event description, Domain and record ID, Action name, Recipient emails, A link to the event.

Important Notes
• `Parameter Required`: Size checking only occurs if attachExceededHandling is provided (not null/empty)
• `Default Strip Behavior`: When unconfigured but limit exceeded, attachments are automatically stripped and email still sends
• `Option 2 Creates Draft`: When "2" is used, email content is saved as a draft record on the parent entity for reference
• `System Users Excluded`: Notification emails are NOT sent if event was triggered by a system process user
• `Link Alternative`: System may convert attachments to download links if SendAttachmentsAsLinksIfExceedMaxSize is enabled
• `Attachment Types`: Only applies to actual file attachments, not inline images or embedded content
• `Multiple Attachment Sources`: All attachment sources (folder, filter, parent filter, static files) are included in size calculation

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description:
Tasks can only be attached to domains where `HasTasks = true`.

When a domain supports tasks (`HasTasks = true`):

  • Task is created and linked to the parent record through ParentDomainID and ParentID
  • Task appears in the parent record's task list
  • Behavior works as expected

When a domain does not support tasks (`HasTasks = false`):

  • Task is still created as a standalone task
  • Task is not attached to the triggering record (no ParentDomainID or ParentID linkage)
  • Task exists in the system but is orphaned and not visible from the parent record

Special handling for Custom Entities:

Custom entities (client-defined domains) can specify a ParentTaskHost property that points to a related parent domain that supports tasks. In this case:

  • Task is attached to the configured parent domain instead
  • Example: A custom Review entity may attach tasks to its parent Claim

owner.description:
The owner field assigns the task to a user. It accepts:

  • a numeric UserID
  • standard {formTags}
  • special system tags ({User}, {User.SupervisorUser}, {None})
Expand for more details... Recommended Declarative Approach
"owner": "123" | Assigns the task to Origami User ID 123.

Form Tags
"owner": "{Claim.AdjusterID}" | Must resolve to a numeric User ID or a runtime error will occur.

System Tags
"owner": "{None}" | Assigns no owner.
"owner": "{User}" | Uses the User ID derived from the API token.
"owner": "{User.SupervisorUser}" | Uses the supervisor of the user derived from the API token. If none exists, behaves like {None}.

Advanced Options -- Rarely Needed
"owner": "{NamedUser}" | Requires the companion input parameter of ownerNamedUserId.
"owner": "{CustomTagExpression}" | Requires the companion input parameter of ownerCustomTagExpression.

ownerNamedUserId.description: Rarely Used. Only required if `{NamedUser}` is supplied as the value of the `owner` input. This should be a numeric Origami User ID.

ownerCustomTagExpression.description:
Rarely used. This field is only required when {CustomTagExpression} is supplied as the value of the owner input.

Expand for more details... Purpose
Enables dynamic user assignment using nested object navigation, also known as property path expressions.

Example
{
  "owner": "{CustomTagExpression}",
  "ownerCustomTagExpression": "Claim.Location.CustomUser1ID"
}
Usage Guidance
This capability exists primarily to support legacy applications. For API development, using form tags or explicitly declared User IDs for the owner input is strongly recommended. These approaches are simpler, more predictable, and make this field unnecessary in most cases.

backupOwner.description:
The backupOwner specifies which user serves as the backup/secondary assignee for the task. Works identically to owner but assigns the backup user role. It accepts values of:

  • a numeric UserID
  • standard {formTags}
  • special system tags ({User}, {User.SupervisorUser}, {None})

See 'owner' for more details

backupOwnerNamedUserId.description: Rarely Used. Only required if `{NamedUser}` is supplied as the value of the `backupOwner` input. This should be a numeric Origami User ID.

backupOwnerCustomTagExpression.description:

Usage Guidance

dueDate.description:
This value specifies when the created task should be due. It's an optional string parameter that supports multiple formats including fixed dates, relative date expressions, and form tags. The system uses sophisticated date parsing logic that handles date math, natural language date expressions, and integrates with non-working day configurations.

For a detailed guide on the dueDate input, click here

relativeToDate.description:
This optional value influences how the dueDate field is calculated and interpreted.

For a detailed guide on the dueDate input, click here

hoursOffset.description:
This optional value influences how the dueDate field is calculated and interpreted.

For a detailed guide on the dueDate input, click here

minutesOffset.description:
This optional value influences how the dueDate field is calculated and interpreted.

For a detailed guide on the dueDate input, click here

dueTime.description:
This value specifies the time of day when the task is due, using military time format (24-hour clock without colons). It works in conjunction with `dueDate` to set a complete due date/time for the task.

Military time is represented as a 4-digit number where:
• First 2 digits = Hour (00-23)
• Last 2 digits = Minutes (00-59)

Expand for more samples of Military Time and Offsets... 
  "dueTime": 0       // 12:00 AM (midnight)
  "dueTime": 100     // 1:00 AM
  "dueTime": 830     // 8:30 AM
  "dueTime": 1200    // 12:00 PM (noon)
  "dueTime": 1430    // 2:30 PM
  "dueTime": 1700    // 5:00 PM
  "dueTime": 2359    // 11:59 PM
}

If dueTime is not provided but hoursOffset or minutesOffset are specified, the system automatically calculates the due time in relation to the moment in time when the API request is executed.
Example:
{
  "hoursOffset": 48,
  "minutesOffset": 30,
  "dueTimeZone": "Eastern Standard Time"
}
If executed at 10:00 AM EST on Monday, this creates a task due at 12:30 PM EST on Wednesday (48 hours 30 minutes later).

dueTimeZone.description:
This value pecifies which timezone to use when calculating due times from `hoursOffset`/`minutesOffset`. It ensures time calculations respect the task owner's timezone, not just the server's local time.

If `null` or not provided, the default timezone will be the server's system timezone setting

Note: The system automatically handles daylight saving time (DST) adjustments based on the timezone selected.

If your timezone is not in the enum list, use any valid **Windows timezone ID**.

taskCategoryId.description: This value specifies which Task Category to assign to the created task. Task Categories are user-defined classifications that help organize and categorize tasks within the system. They can be configured to apply only to specific domains (e.g., Claims, Policies) and major coverages (e.g., Workers' Compensation, General Liability), with role-based permissions controlling who can view and create tasks in each category.

priority.description:
Sets the urgency level of the task, helping users identify which tasks need immediate attention versus those that can be addressed later. Priority is a visual indicator displayed in the UI with icons/colors to quickly distinguish high-priority tasks from normal or low-priority ones.
• High ("H") - Most urgent
• Normal ("N") - Standard
• Low ("L") - Least urgent
• null - No priority (treated as Normal)

shared.description:
This value controls task visibility and determines who can view and edit the task beyond the task creator, owner, and backup owner.

• "P" (Private) |Only visible to task creator, assigned owner, backup owner, and users with "View Private Task" permission
• "R" (Shared but View Only) | Visible to all users with task viewing permissions, but read-only for non-owners
• "S" (Shared) | Visible and editable by all users with task editing permissions

projectId.description:
This value associates a task with a project, enabling project-based task tracking and organization. Projects are standalone entities used to manage collections of related tasks, similar to workflows or initiatives.

Important: projectId is distinct from RiskProject (ERM projects used in risk management). Standard Projects are general-purpose task management containers, while RiskProjects are part of the Enhanced ERM module for risk mitigation tracking.

Leave `null` for routine operational tasks.

attachToParent.description:
Mutual Exclusivity Warning: The attachToParent and attachToParentOfParent options cannot both be set to true.

When attachToParent is set to true, the task is linked directly to the triggering record, provided that the triggering record’s domain supports tasks.

When to Use attachToParent:

  • The event originates from a primary domain that supports tasks (for example, Claims, Policies, or Locations)
  • The task is directly associated with the triggering record itself
  • This is the default and recommended choice for most scenarios

attachToParentOfParent.description:
Mutual Exclusivity Warning: The attachToParentOfParent and attachToParent options cannot both be set to true.

When attachToParent is set to true, the task is linked directly to the triggering record, provided that the triggering record’s domain supports tasks.

When to Use attachToParent:

  • Event is on child domain without task support (Transactions, Benefits, CheckPayments)
  • Task should be visible on parent record's task list
  • Need to associate with higher-level entity

isRecurring.description:
Enables automatic creation of recurring tasks. When `true`, the system automatically generates a new task whenever the current task is marked complete, based on the specified frequency and conditions.

If isRecurring is true, both `recurringFrequency` and `recurringFreqBasedOn` must be provided.

recurringFreqBasedOn.description:
When isRecurring is true, the recurringFreqBasedOn field is required.

Common Values (available in most or all installations):

  • DueDate — The original due date of the task
  • CompleteDate — The date the task was completed
  • EntryDate — The date the task was created
  • ModifiedDate — The date the task was last modified

Client-Specific Values (may vary by installation):

  • CustomDate1 through CustomDate20, if configured for the client’s Task domain
  • Any additional custom date fields defined in the Task domain metadata

recurringFrequency.description:
Requirement: When isRecurring is set to true, the recurringFrequency field is required.

The recurringFrequency value is a date expression that determines when the next recurring task is due. The expression is applied relative to the date specified by recurringFreqBasedOn.

Supported Expressions

Relative date expressions use + notation with an optional unit suffix. 

"recurringFrequency": "+30d"   // 30 days after the base date
"recurringFrequency": "+1m"    // 1 month after the base date
"recurringFrequency": "+1bm"   // Beginning of the next month
"recurringFrequency": "+1y"    // 1 year after the base date
"recurringFrequency": "+2w"    // 2 weeks after the base date

Learn more about supported date expressions

recurrConditionFilter.description:
Optional. This filter expression conditionally determines whether a new recurring task should be created when a recurring task is completed.

The expression is evaluated against the completed task using Origami’s Advanced Filter syntax. If the filter evaluates to true, the next recurring task is created. If it evaluates to false, no new task is generated.

This is the same filter syntax used by the /api/{domain}/Query endpoint.

Expand for more info on Filtering Syntax...

Supported Operators

Operator Description Example
eq Equals (or IN for multiple values) Status:eq:"Active"
!eq Not equals Status:!eq:"Closed"
lt Less than Priority:lt:"H"
lte Less than or equal to DaysOpen:lte:30
gt Greater than DaysOpen:gt:7
gte Greater than or equal to DaysOpen:gte:1
between Between two values DueDate:between:Today,+30d
!between Not between two values DueDate:!between:Yesterday,Today
startswith String starts with Description:startswith:"Monthly"
contains String contains Description:contains:"Review"
empty Field is null or empty CompleteDate:empty
!empty Field is not null or empty AssignedToID:!empty
true Boolean field is true IsRecurring:true
false Boolean field is false IsClosed:false
trueorempty Boolean field is true or null IsRecurring:trueorempty
falseorempty Boolean field is false or null IsClosed:falseorempty
me User field matches the current user AssignedToUser:me

Supported Field References

Common Task Fields

  • Status — Task status
  • Priority — Task priority (H / N / L)
  • DueDate — Task due date
  • CompleteDate — Completion date
  • AssignedToID — Assigned user ID
  • AssignedToUser — Assigned user (used with :me)
  • TaskCategoryID — Task category
  • ProjectID — Associated project
  • Description — Task description
  • Shared — Visibility (P / R / S)
  • CustomDate1, CustomDate2, etc. — Custom date fields
  • CustomText1, CustomText2, etc. — Custom text fields

Related Domain Fields (via dot notation)

  • Project.Status — Project status (when associated)
  • Member.Status — Member status (when associated)
  • Any related domain field accessible from the Task context

recurrConditionViewId.description:
Alternative to recurrConditionFilter. This option uses a saved View’s filter expression to conditionally determine whether a new recurring task should be created when a recurring task is completed.

When recurrConditionViewId is provided, the system retrieves the FilterString from the specified View and evaluates it against the completed task.

Evaluation Behavior

  • When a recurring task is completed, the system checks whether recurrConditionViewId has a value
  • If present, the system loads the View’s FilterString from the Views table and evaluates it against the completed task
  • If the filter evaluates to false, no new recurring task is created
  • If the filter evaluates to true, the next recurring task is created

Precedence Rules

  • When both recurrConditionViewId and recurrConditionFilter are provided, recurrConditionViewId takes precedence

Usage Requirements

  • The referenced View must belong to the Task domain (DomainID = 7)
  • The View must be accessible to the system and does not need to be user‑specific

noSendIfEmptyTo.description:
If all recipient fields resolve to empty values after form tag processing, the action silently succeeds. This behavior results in the following:

  • No email is sent
  • Email generation returns null without throwing an exception
  • The surrounding event or workflow continues without failure

This prevents the email action from causing an error when the to, cc, and bcc fields all resolve to empty strings. It is especially useful when recipients are supplied via dynamic form tags that may not always have values.

letterTemplateId.description:
When letterTemplateId is provided, the system:
1) Retrieves the LetterTemplate by ID from the database
2) Processes any merge fields within the template using data from the domain record
3) Converts the formatted document content to HTML
4) The rendered output of the letter template is used either as A) a replacement of the email body or B) a supplement to the email body (depending on configuration settings)
If letterTemplateId is NOT provided: The body parameter is used directly as the email content

emailTypeId.description:
While this input value is optional, it is strongly recommended. You CAN omit `emailTypeId` if:
The user has full email access (admin/unrestricted), OR
The user's EmailRole has CanAccessEmailsWithoutEmailType = true

You MUST provide emailTypeId if:
The user has restricted email access (assigned to an EmailRole)
AND that EmailRole has CanAccessEmailsWithoutEmailType = false (or null)

Omitting this value when it is otherwise needed can cause the action to be queued, but it could still fail at runtime execution due to a security/permission error.

attachFilesFromFolderId.description:
Optional parameter that specifies a Folder ID. When provided, all files from that folder will be attached to the email.
Important: If any of the following inputs are provided, they take precedence and `attachFilesFromFolderId` is completely ignored:
• `attachFilesFromFilter`
• `attachFilesFromParentFilter`
• `attachStaticFiles`

attachFilesFromFilter.description:
Optional parameter that accepts a filter expression string to specify which files attached to the domain record should be automatically attached to the email. Uses Origami's Advanced Search filter syntax.

`1)` Applies the filter expression to the File records attached to the domain record
`2)`Retrieves all files matching the filter criteria
`3)`Automatically attaches those files to the outgoing email

Attachment Aggregation Rules
Files selected by this parameter are added cumulatively with files produced by the other attachment filtering mechanisms. All files are combined and deduplicated prior to sending the email. The final set of attached files is the union of files returned by the following parameters:
`attachFilesFromFilter`, `attachFilesFromParentFilter`, and `attachStaticFiles`

If the same file is selected by more than one of these sources, it is included only once in the outgoing email.

attachFilesFromParentFilter.description:
An Origami Advanced Search filter expression to attach files from parent records of the triggering entity. Uses the same filter syntax as `attachFilesFromFilter`, but searches in the parent record(s) instead of the current record.

When this parameter is provided:

`1)` Identifies all parent records linked to the triggering entity (via the Link table)
`2)` For each parent that supports file attachments (`HasFiles=true`)
`3)` Applies the filter expression to find matching files attached to that parent
`4)` Returns the union of all matching files from all parents

Attachment Aggregation Rules
Files selected by this parameter are added cumulatively with files produced by the other attachment filtering mechanisms. All files are combined and deduplicated prior to sending the email. The final set of attached files is the union of files returned by the following parameters:
`attachFilesFromFilter`, `attachFilesFromParentFilter`, and `attachStaticFiles`

If the same file is selected by more than one of these sources, it is included only once in the outgoing email.

attachStaticFiles.description:
A comma-separated list of File IDs representing specific files that already exist in the Origami system. These files will be attached to the email regardless of their location or parent record. The files are directly referenced by their corresponding `FileID`.

Attachment Aggregation Rules
Files selected by this parameter are added cumulatively with files produced by the other attachment filtering mechanisms. All files are combined and deduplicated prior to sending the email. The final set of attached files is the union of files returned by the following parameters:
`attachFilesFromFilter`, `attachFilesFromParentFilter`, and `attachStaticFiles`

If the same file is selected by more than one of these sources, it is included only once in the outgoing email.

trackReplies.description:
Enables reply tracking for the email, allowing the system to capture and record recipient responses as new Email records in Origami. When enabled, the system generates a unique tracking address that recipient replies are sent to, which then get processed and attached to the original email's parent record.

Important Notes
• System Configuration Required - Email infrastructure must be configured to receive emails at the tracking address domain.
• Recorded Emails Only - Only works if system is configured to record outgoing emails (RecordOutgoingEmails setting)
• Thread Matching - Replies are matched by ThreadGuid, not email subject or message threading
• File Attachments - Reply email attachments are automatically processed and attached to the reply Email record

sendUnsecure.description:
Bypasses email encryption and sends the email without secure/encrypted delivery, even when encryption is configured for the system. This parameter allows users with proper permissions to override encryption settings on a per-email basis.

Important Notes
• Audit Trail - The SendUnsecure value is stored on the Email record for compliance auditing
• Permission Required - Users must have explicit permission to send unsecured emails
• System Override - Some email templates can force encryption (SecureEmailOption = "F") which prevents this parameter from working

usePlainText.description:
Controls whether the email is sent as plain text or HTML. When set to true, the email body is sent as plain text without HTML formatting. When false (default), the email supports HTML markup.

Form Tags: Both plain text and HTML bodies support Origami form tags (e.g., {ClaimNumber}, {UserEmail})
Automatic Encoding: When HTML mode is on, plain text content is automatically HTML-encoded to prevent formatting issues

doNotRecordEmail.description:
Prevents the system from creating an Email record in the database for this sent email. When set to true, the email is sent but no record is saved to the Emails table or linked to the parent record.

Important: This parameter only has effect when the system-wide setting RecordOutgoingEmails is enabled.

excludeGlobalSignature.description: When set to `true`, the global email signature that would normally be appended to all outgoing emails from the system is ommitted.

priority.description:
The priority parameter is a boolean flag that marks the email as high priority, which affects how the email appears to recipients in the email client.

When set to `true`, the email is sent with high priority status, which typically displays a red exclamation mark or similar indicator in most email clients to signal urgency to recipients.

If priority is `false` or omitted (default), emails are sent with normal priority

attachExceededHandling.description:
`"" (empty)` or `null` -- Default: Send email without attachments (standard behavior)
`1` -- Send & Notify: Send email without attachments AND notify* the user who triggered the event
`2` -- Notify But Don't Send: Do NOT send email, create draft email record on parent, AND notify* the user

*Notifications include:Client name, Event description, Domain and record ID, Action name, Recipient emails, A link to the event.

Important Notes
• `Parameter Required`: Size checking only occurs if attachExceededHandling is provided (not null/empty)
• `Default Strip Behavior`: When unconfigured but limit exceeded, attachments are automatically stripped and email still sends
• `Option 2 Creates Draft`: When "2" is used, email content is saved as a draft record on the parent entity for reference
• `System Users Excluded`: Notification emails are NOT sent if event was triggered by a system process user
• `Link Alternative`: System may convert attachments to download links if SendAttachmentsAsLinksIfExceedMaxSize is enabled
• `Attachment Types`: Only applies to actual file attachments, not inline images or embedded content
• `Multiple Attachment Sources`: All attachment sources (folder, filter, parent filter, static files) are included in size calculation
